title: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain on the sale of depreciated real property
rule: Section 1250 treats gain on depreciable realty as ordinary income up to additional depreciation, all of it for most property. Additional depreciation is all depreciation for property held one year or less; if longer, only the excess over straight line, so a straight-line building has none. Unrecaptured section 1250 gain is long-term capital gain, not otherwise ordinary, that would be ordinary if section 1250 reached all depreciation at 100 percent, less any excess of net short-term capital loss, collectibles loss and long-term loss carryover over collectibles and section 1202 gain. Its top rate, for individuals, estates and trusts, is 25 percent. Allowable depreciation counts unless records show less allowed.
changeWatch: Amendments to the capital gains rate structure in section 1(h), including the 25 percent rate in 1(h)(1)(E) and the definition in 1(h)(6), or to the definition of additional depreciation in section 1250(b).
